title: Reformed should not over-read Bellarmine ignorance over science line
source_text: LXIV. Et similiter Reformati Scholae Romanae Doctoribus imputare non debent, quod ad fidem privatorum nullam rerum credendarum cognitionem requirant, & quod in iis rerum divinarum ignorantiam illarum scientiae atque cognitioni praeferendam censeant. Ac supra modum videntur exagitare illud Bellarmini, nempe, quod fides contra scientiam distinguitur, & quod fides melius per ignorantiam, quam per scientiam definitur. Etenim licet istud dure atque incommode dictum sit, ex Bellarmini tamen sensu, per hoc nihil significatur, quod ab ipsa Reformatorum doctrina dissentiat, ut patet ex iis quae antea fuerunt exposita. Ubi ostendimus Bellarminum scientiam ibi proprie sumere pro notitia quadam evidenti, qualem non habemus respectu eorum quae ad fidem pertinent.
pass_a_gloss: And likewise the Reformed ought not to impute to the Doctors of the Roman school that for the faith of private persons they require no cognition of things to be believed, and that in them they judge ignorance of divine things preferable to science and cognition of them. And they seem to rail beyond measure at that saying of Bellarmine, namely that faith is distinguished against science, and that faith is better defined by ignorance than by science. For although that is said harshly and inconveniently, yet in Bellarmine sense nothing is signified by it that dissents from the Reformed doctrine itself, as is clear from what was set out before. Where we showed that Bellarmine there takes science properly for a certain evident knowledge, such as we do not have with respect to things that belong to faith.
pass_b_english: Reformed should not charge Rome with requiring zero cognition for private faith or preferring ignorance to knowledge.
Bellarmine faith better by ignorance than science is harsh phrasing, but means science as evident knowledge we lack regarding faith-objects — not dissent from Reformed doctrine.

lemmas.latin: melius per ignorantiam, quam per scientiam
lemmas.gloss: better by ignorance than by science

choices.why: Harsh Bellarmine line = non-evident faith, not praise of ignorance.
rejected: Bellarmine prefers unbelief or blank minds
